sections.h2: Where a Morrow County deed is recorded
sections.html:
The recorder's office, inside the courthouse at 48 E. High St., Mt. Gilead, OH 43338, takes deeds and mortgages for recording. Phone 419-947-3060. Weekday counter hours run from 8 to 4. More is on the recorder's page.

Sellers in Cardington, Marengo, Edison and the townships make the same trip to Mt. Gilead. To skip the drive, have an electronic recording company file for you (see below).

The documents-filed list is broad. Sellers of a house, including an inherited one, usually need one of these entries:

  • Deeds, including warranty, quit claim, survivorship and sheriff's deeds.
  • Mortgages, along with releases, assignments, assumptions and subordinations.
  • Land contracts, leases, easements and powers of attorney.
  • Trusts, affidavits and certificates of transfer.
  • Liens of several kinds, such as mechanic's liens, notices of commencement and federal or personal tax liens.

Plats, condominium filings, annexations and zoning resolutions are on the list as well, so the same office holds the map side of the county's land records.

E-recording has been open for every document type since September 8, 2025. Four vendors can help: CSC, Simplifile, ePN and Indecomm. Most title companies and closing attorneys keep an account with at least one, which means a seller seldom signs up alone.

Record searching moved to a different system in the same period. The records search page sends visitors to RecordHub, where you must create a login before you can look anything up. The account costs nothing, and the login requirement protects the records from cyberattacks.

sections.h2: What the auditor does before the recorder
sections.html:
Under section 319.20, the county auditor moves the parcel into the new owner's name and endorses the deed. Before that, the incoming owner or an agent for that owner files a statement of value as described in section 319.202, electronically or in three paper copies.

The statement carries two questions that matter to a Morrow seller. Has the property received a tax reduction for owner-occupied homes? And was the land ever enrolled in the Current Agricultural Use Valuation program? If the answer to the second is yes, the statement must note that the land can face a recoupment charge when it stops qualifying.

The Morrow County Auditor's conveyance fee page shows $4.00 per thousand for both real estate and manufactured homes. The grantor pays it, together with the 50 cent transfer fee that section 319.54(G)(2) sets for each parcel entered.

Prices for the basic filing are not the recorder's to set. Section 317.32 prescribes a base fee and an equal housing trust fund fee, and the office may add an optional preservation surcharge capped at five dollars, which the county keeps for general use. Pay when you hand the paper in. Electronic filers may pay later by electronic funds transfer or a similar method.

Exhibits push the page count up, and the price follows. Get a page count from the title agent ahead of closing so the check matches.

sections.h2: Transfers that owe no conveyance fee
sections.html:
Plenty of transfers skip the auditor's fee under state law. Family and estate sales run into these most:

  • Corrective or confirming deeds for something already on record.
  • Spouse-to-spouse gifts, and gifts from a mother or father to a son or daughter.
  • Heirs or devisees of one decedent passing property among themselves for no money.
  • A deed placing property in a revocable trust, and the deed taking it back out.
  • Any no-payment transfer that does not count as a gift.
  • Paperwork that only secures or releases a debt.

An exempt filing has to spell out why. Not sure a family deed qualifies? Ring the auditor before anything goes to the recorder.

The grantor signs the deed and acknowledges that signature before an authorized officer, as section 5301.01 directs. The list covers a court judge or clerk, a county auditor or engineer, a notary public and a mayor. Most sellers simply see a notary at the title company or a bank.

A mortgage paid off at closing leaves one more task for the lender. Section 5301.36 gives the mortgagee ninety days after satisfaction to record the release. Look in the recorder's index a few weeks later to be sure it is there.

Property Check is a free fraud alert service run by the recorder. Subscribers hear when any document is filed against a named property, so a forged deed or fake lien gets noticed fast. It is a good fit for a vacant house or an estate property, where no one is collecting the mail.

Alerts do not replace a periodic look at the record. A quick RecordHub search under your own name every so often costs only the time it takes to log in.

Central Ohio's Morrow County, part of the Columbus metro area, has an estimated 36,305 residents in 14,981 housing units for 2025. Homeowners live in 81.2 percent of the homes, at a median value of $222,300. With that much owner-held housing, ordinary owner-to-owner sales fill most of the recorder's deed work.

sections.h2: What belongs in the packet before closing
sections.html:
Start with a deed whose grantor name matches the last recorded deed letter for letter. The auditor's transfer step keys off the earlier instrument, so a spelling mismatch or a missing citation to it can stall the filing. Pack the full legal description, the grantee's mailing address and the signed statement of value.

Check, too, whether the parcel ever sat in the farm-use program. Applying costs a one-time $25, and the cutoff is the first Monday of March. Pulling land out triggers a recoupment charge equal to three years of savings, so a seller carving off a few farm acres should ask how the split changes it.

Last, find out who files the paperwork and how. Paper deeds work through the courthouse offices in sequence, while e-recorded ones move through the vendor's system, and the route tells you when the recorded copy will arrive.

Selling for cash trims the list. No lender means no new mortgage to record and no payoff release to chase, so the deed, the statement of value and the conveyance fee are usually the whole filing. Keep a copy of the recorded deed with your closing papers once it comes back.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Morrow County recorder?
faqs.a: Dial 419-947-3060. The counter sits in the courthouse at 48 E. High St. in Mt. Gilead and closes at four on weekdays.

faqs.q: Does Morrow County accept deeds filed online?
faqs.a: Yes, through electronic recording vendors: CSC, Simplifile, ePN and Indecomm. E-recording has covered all documents since September 8, 2025.

faqs.q: What is the Morrow County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The county auditor charges $4.00 per thousand. The grantor pays it at the auditor's office, along with a 50 cent per parcel transfer fee set by state law.

faqs.q: Do I need an account to search Morrow County land records online?
faqs.a: Yes. The records search now runs through RecordHub, and users create a free login. The step protects the records from cyberattacks.

faqs.q: Is a deed between family members free of the conveyance fee?
faqs.a: Some are. State law exempts gifts between spouses and between a parent and child, and transfers among heirs of one decedent for no money. The filing must state the exemption, so check with the auditor first.
